body.purpose: Default terminal monospace, regular weight. The base layer for all output.

emphasis.purpose: ANSI bold (\033[1m). Reserved for status-line phrases and user-typeable commands per the Bold-Is-A-Command Rule.

breakpoints.name: tty
breakpoints.purpose: When stdout is a terminal: ANSI colors and emoji are eligible (subject to --colors / --no-emoji).

breakpoints.name: pipe
breakpoints.purpose: When stdout is not a terminal: ANSI off, emoji still eligible per --emoji, output stays grep-friendly.

narrative.overview: lnk's interface is the terminal, and the terminal owes the user the truth about their filesystem and Git state. Every line of output exists because something happened on disk; nothing exists to fill space. The voice is calm, declarative, and short. Color and emoji are functional cues, not decoration: a green check means a write succeeded, a red parenthetical means a list entry is broken, a cyan path means "this is the file in your managed repo." If the terminal is colorless or the user passed --no-emoji or --quiet, the words alone must still carry the meaning. The system rejects verbose enterprise CLIs in the Terraform/AWS lineage and festive npm-style output. Hierarchy is built without graphical chrome: indentation marks belonging, blank lines mark sections, gray marks detail, bold marks the user-typeable command.
keyCharacteristics: Truthful: every line maps to a filesystem or Git state change.
Terse: no preamble, no internal monologue, no narration.
Inspectable: output is grep-friendly; meaning never depends on color alone.
Trust-aware: warnings name the file and the recovery path (.lnk-backup).
Pipe-safe: ANSI, emoji, and animation are skipped when stdout is not a TTY or when the user opts out.

rules.name: The Address Rule
rules.body: Cyan is exclusively the address of a managed path. Never apply cyan to messages, hints, or status. If you find cyan on a verb or a sentence, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Outcome Rule
rules.body: Green is reserved for user-visible state changes that completed. It is not 'everything went fine'; it is 'this thing exists now / is healthy now.' Status reports without a state change should not be green.

rules.name: The No-Color-Alone Rule
rules.body: No piece of meaning is carried by color alone. Errors have the word 'error' or ❌; warnings have the word 'warning' or ⚠️; managed paths are recognizable as paths regardless of cyan. --colors never and NO_COLOR must produce output that conveys identical information.

rules.name: The One-Emoji Rule
rules.body: Each output line carries at most one leading emoji glyph. No combinations, no inline emoji mid-sentence, no decorative trailing glyphs.

rules.name: The Bold-Is-A-Command Rule
rules.body: Bold body weight is reserved for text the user can copy and run (lnk push, lnk add --host work <file>, bootstrap.sh). Bold is not for emphasis on adjectives or feelings. If it isn't a command or a literal filename, it isn't bold.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. No box drawing, no ===== separators, no banners. Hierarchy comes from leading spaces and blank lines.

rules.name: The Two-Space Indent Rule
rules.body: Sub-lines under a status line indent exactly two spaces. Not four, not a tab, not aligned-to-emoji. Two spaces is the system's only structural offset.

rules.name: The Quiet-Success Rule
rules.body: A command that did exactly what the user asked, with no surprises and no side-effects worth surfacing, may exit silently (or with the smallest possible status line). Silence is a valid success state when --quiet is set.

rules.name: The Pair-Then-Indent Rule
rules.body: A status line and its detail lines are a unit. The detail lines are always indented; the status line is never indented. If you find an indented headline or a flush-left sub-detail, the unit was assembled wrong.

dos: Do make every line of output map to a filesystem or Git state change, an actionable hint, or a recoverable warning.
Do carry meaning in the words first, then layer color and emoji as cues. Verify: --colors never --no-emoji output reads identically.
Do use Success(...) (✅ + green + bold) only for confirmed state changes, not for 'everything is fine' status checks (use Plain(...) for those, or just no output).
Do use cyan exclusively for managed-path addresses (Link, Colored(..., ColorCyan)).
Do end hint chains with a Bold(...) user-typeable command.
Do indent every sub-line two spaces under its status line.
Do honor NO_COLOR, --colors never, --no-emoji, and --quiet/-q in every new command, and verify with non-TTY pipes.
Do name the file and the recovery path (.lnk-backup) in any warning that touched the filesystem.
donts: Don't narrate. No Initializing…, no Loading…, no Checking…, no DEBUG/INFO noise on success. PRODUCT.md is explicit: lnk is not verbose enterprise tooling.
Don't add new uses of Sparkles(✨), Rocket(🚀), or Target(🎯). They are documented as legacy vocabulary; reach for Success(...) or Plain(...) instead.
Don't stack multiple emoji on a line. One leading glyph maximum; never inline mid-sentence; never trailing decoration.
Don't rely on color to carry meaning. No 'the green line means it worked' without the word.
Don't introduce ASCII art, banners, box-drawing characters, ===== separators, or progress bars. The Flat-By-Default Rule excludes them.
Don't apply bold to adjectives, feelings, or non-typeable text. Bold is for commands and literal filenames only (the Bold-Is-A-Command Rule).
Don't indent at four spaces or with a tab. Two spaces is the only structural offset.
Don't print partial-color in non-TTY pipes. If the writer's output is not a terminal, ANSI is off — full stop.
Don't invent new component shapes inline. If a command needs a new pattern, add it to the Components section first, then implement.
Don't swallow detail in --quiet. Quiet means no output, not some output, less colorful. Exit code carries success or failure.
